messages.subject: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.subject_clean: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats team,

I am using the Skyline tool for biological significance analysis using the group comparison feature and I noticed something unexpected to me: the TestingResult.csv file contains proteins which have data only for one biological replicate from within the two compared experimental conditions. They contain p-values and other statistics. I was surprised since I thought that MSstats will exclude such proteins from further statistical analysis since there is no information regarding their biological variability, and thus they are unsuitable for testing biological hypotheses. Please let me know if I have misunderstood something, and if there is a way to filter out those proteins from the result file.

Thank you very much in advance!

messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.subject_clean: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.body_plain:
I'm not 100% sure about your experimental design. But, generally, MSstats can test with one biological replicate, if there is any other technical replicate. Linear model will include only 'Group' term. If you use Skyline external tool, it is not easy to manipulate the data. What I have in mind is that you can uncheck the protein that has one biological replicate manually. If you use R, you can remove them easily.

Hope to help.

messages.subject: Re: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.subject_clean: Biological significance analysis using a single biological replicate
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the reply Meena!

My data does not have any technical replicates (multiple injections of the same sample), so maybe what you are saying is that linear models can use the variance between the selected features within a single biological replicate data (red box in attached figure) for its biological variance? I would normally assume you would have to derive biological variance from within data of biological replicates (green box). The figures shows 6 different experimental conditions, each had 4 biological replicates. As you can see, there is only one biological replicate for the right-most condition and I am wondering where does the variance for this condition come from to perform biological significance analysis.

I might have misunderstood something. I would appreciate if you could direct me towards some material to understand this better.

Thanks again!

Hi all,

I have been trying to run MSstats on our Progenesis files.
Since our files are lack of spectral count, peptide sequences, modification etc columns, I assumed at the beginning that the script will not work.
And as expected we got an error

For future we can export the data with all required columns but for time being we don't have this option. Therefore;

1- If I introduce these columns with fake values, what would happen? Or for which ones introducing fake values will have no effect on the outcome?
2- Is there are way to modify the code such that "accession","peptide count","unique peptides", "confidence score", "anova(p)", "max fold change", "highest mean condition",
"lowest mean condition", "description", "normalized abundance", "raw abundance" with corresponding runnames and condition columns would be enough?
Thank you very much for your effort and your help.

Best,
Canan

messages.subject: Re: Error while reading Progenesis output
messages.body_plain:
First of all, there are small updated in v3.8.x from Bioconductor.

At least you need 'Sequence', 'Charge'  columns. For Sequence column, I recommend to used 'Accession', which will be protein id. For Charge column, I recommend just one unique value, such as 0 for all.
At this moment, you need 'Spectral.count' columns. You don't need all. Just add one Spectral.count column at the end.

- Meena

messages.subject: Volcano plots for Log2FC of Inf and -Inf values
messages.subject_clean: Volcano plots for Log2FC of Inf and -Inf values
messages.body_plain:
When using MSstats to process DDA data you often get missing values in one condition or another that result in Log2FC of Inf, -Inf, or NA.  When plotting such volcano plots, you end up with a bunch of dots up in the corners.  I think it would be great to have an option in the volcano plots to exclude proteins for a given comparision plot for which the Log2FC is Inf, -Inf, or NA.

-Danielle

messages.subject: Re: Volcano plots for Log2FC of Inf and -Inf values
messages.subject_clean: Volcano plots for Log2FC of Inf and -Inf values
messages.body_plain:
Here is temporary solution. You can filter out the testing result with any issue before drawing volcano plot.

test <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix=comparison, data=QuantData)

test2 <- test$ComparisonResult[is.na(test$ComparisonResult$issue), ]

groupComparisonPlots(data=test2, type="VolcanoPlot")

Hope to help.
- Meena
